context:
Goal: q_max lanes #1036, #1038, #1037 and #1039 merge without waiting hours on a browser run that keeps failing.
Problem (risk): q_max's merge tool refuses to merge onto a red main. #1036 (lane qmax-browser-prod-build) is the browser-tier fix itself. Auto mode refused the coordinator's ruling to merge it with --base-red-ok as a CI bypass, so the call is yours.
Based on (measured): runner 9 read main's last four browser runs: three were cancelled at 2.5-3 h and one failed at 3.5 h. The current run, 42274824088, had run 110 min at 14:48 CST.
Departs from: main, where merges wait for a green base — merges #1036 alone onto a red base.
Meanwhile: runner 9 waits on main's browser run.
holds: Whether q_max #1036 may merge onto a red main.
lane: coordinator: runner 9 merges #1036 with the reason flag; closes when #1036 merges

lastAnswer.note: why does q_max use a unique merge tool? but ya merge it

options.gain: The fix lands today, and the queue moves.
options.how: Only if the failing job in main's last ended run is the one #1036 changes: #1036 merges alone with --base-red-ok, which you type. Then one browser run on main, and the other three merge only on its green.
options.label: Merge #1036 alone onto red
options.lose: One merge onto a red base.

options.how: Wait for run 42274824088 and each later run.
options.label: Wait for green
options.lose: Perhaps hours, and a red end blocks all four.

reply: Routed 15:19 CST to the coordinator and runner 9: #1036 merges onto the red main, with your save as the reason. q_max uses the same shared merge tool as every repo. The red-main refusal is that tool's rule (decision no-merge-onto-red-main). This item closes when #1036 merges.
title: q_max: merge the browser-tier fix #1036 alone onto a red main?
why: Four q_max lanes wait on a green browser run on main, and none of the last four runs ended green.
